note_claims.claim: The patient is presenting with a flare of rheumatoid arthritis lasting three weeks.
The patient reports painful swelling of the right wrist and right hand knuckles for three weeks.
The patient reports early morning stiffness lasting about 30 minutes.
The patient reports mild foot ache.
The patient reports mild nausea the day after taking methotrexate.
The patient denies sore throat, fever, bruising, cough, or breathlessness.
The patient drinks about six units of alcohol per week.
The patient had shingles last month.
The patient is prescribed methotrexate 15 mg once weekly on Mondays.
The patient is prescribed folic acid 5 mg once weekly on Thursdays.
The patient has a history of a rash associated with sulfasalazine.
The examination reveals synovitis of the right wrist and the right second and third MCP joints.
The left hand examination is normal.
The chest is clear on auscultation.
The patient's CRP is 28.
The patient's blood count and liver tests are normal.
The disease activity score (DAS28) is 4.8, indicating moderate activity.
The clinical impression is a rheumatoid arthritis flare with moderate disease activity on methotrexate.
The plan is to increase methotrexate to 20 mg once weekly on Mondays.
The plan is to continue folic acid 5 mg once weekly on Thursdays.
The plan is to administer a steroid injection (methylprednisolone 120 mg) today.
The plan is to repeat blood tests every two weeks for the next six weeks, then every three months.
The patient is scheduled for a clinic review in three months.
The patient is advised to stop methotrexate and seek urgent blood tests if they develop a sore throat, fever, mouth ulcers, unusual bruising or bleeding, or a new cough or breathlessness.

transcript_facts.fact: The patient reports bad symptoms for the last three weeks, specifically painful swelling of the right wrist and knuckles on that hand.
The patient reports morning stiffness lasting about half an hour, but corrects this to being longer: 'I can't do my buttons until about half nine, and I get up at eight. So an hour and a half.'
The patient reports that while their feet ache a bit, the primary location of pain is the right hand.
The patient is currently taking methotrexate at a dose of 15 milligrams once a week on Mondays.
The patient is currently taking folic acid at a dose of 5 milligrams once a week on Thursdays.
The patient experiences mild queasiness on Tuesdays, but manages it.
The patient drinks about a glass of wine on Friday and Saturday, totaling about six units of alcohol per week.
The patient has a history of a rash caused by sulfasalazine years ago.
The relative reports that the patient had shingles last month.
The patient confirms having had chickenpox as a child.
Examination findings show synovitis (inflammation of the joint lining) of the right wrist and the right second and third MCP joints.
The patient's CRP is 28, and their blood count and liver tests are normal.
The patient's disease activity score (DAS28) is 4.8, which is classified as moderate activity.
The clinician plans to increase the methotrexate dose to 20 milligrams once a week on Mondays.
The clinician plans to give the patient a steroid injection (methylprednisolone 120 mg) today to settle the flare.
The clinician plans to schedule blood tests every two weeks for the next six weeks, then every three months.
The clinician plans to see the patient back in the clinic in three months.

The clinician provides safety-netting advice: if the patient develops a sore throat, fever, mouth ulcers, unusual bruising or bleeding, or a new cough or breathlessness, they should stop the methotrexate and get an urgent blood test, and call the rheumatology helpline.
